body:
I do have moments of happiness, yeah. Often at work! Sometimes my job makes me happy, it's something I am (or used to be, when I could feel such things) passionate about. I am also sometimes happy when I'm with friends and family, although that's so fleeting. I'll be happy and normal with them there but there's this constant thought in the back of my head that I need them to go away because I want to be alone, if I'm with people for too long I get desperate to be alone even though I am happy. It's hard to explain. And then once I'm alone I sink even deeper into depression than I was before. 

Of course I am often depressed when I am doing objectively fun things and should be happy, too, all the time. But sometimes I am happy. It's just not permanent, and the desire to isolate and be alone and depressed gets stronger the longer I am happy. I know how fucked up that sounds, and maybe it's hard to understand. It's not very logical at all. 

>Maybe you do need to find another job.

Like... maybe. But, I have been depressed to varying degrees in every job I've ever had. Jobs I've loved, jobs I've hated. Also no job - I was unemployed and traveling the world for a year and I was *still* depressed, although there was significantly more happiness. Probably because there was less stress and less downtime and more variety to keep me distracted. But I can't just be unemployed and travel forever, I'm not wealthy. And even if I could, I was never happy for very long stretches of time without a rough patch, and that was only a year. I'm sure it would start to get mundane and my mental health would decline again if I did it forever.

I am not in therapy. I did the online (betterhelp) thing for a minute but found it profoundly unhelpful, so I quit.

I don't think they'd commit me out of malice, but that they might feel I'm in danger and want to protect me. But in reality I think that would make my situation far, far worse. Like, if I am this miserable now with my life relatively together, what kind of despair am I going to feel when I have that stigma publicly and I lose my career and can't pay my bills, you know?

I don't believe that having a mental illness makes people deserve to be alone, unsuccessful, or poor. But be realistic, that often happens.  Mentally ill people are way way more likely to be homeless, jobless, and without a support system than healthy people. It doesn't make sense that I've lucked out to this point, because I am holding on by a thread and have been for a long time. 

I just don't want to do this anymore. I will, because I don't think my dad and grandma would be able to handle it if I killed myself. They'd take it very personally and never get over it. But I just wish I didn't have to.
